This should reveal whether the activation step is irreversible (M6) or reversible (M8), as reversible activation may lead to saturation of active species at high catalyst concentrations.

<hypothesis>
The key difference between M6 and M8 is the reversibility of catalyst activation. M6 has an irreversible activation (cat -> cat*), so all catalyst eventually becomes active, leading to a rate proportional to total catalyst (linear scaling) if activation is fast. M8 has reversible activation (cat <=> cat* + L), so the equilibrium concentration of active cat* may saturate at high total catalyst, causing sublinear scaling. By increasing catalyst concentration to 0.20 M (20 times higher than the first experiment) while keeping substrate at 1.0 M, we can test the scaling. M6 predicts the initial rate will increase roughly 20-fold compared to the cat=0.01 experiment (assuming similar conditions), while M8 predicts a less than 20-fold increase due to equilibrium saturation. The time course will differ accordingly, allowing the fitting to penalize the incorrect scaling. This experiment also maintains substrate at a moderate level to avoid confounding substrate inhibition effects.
</hypothesis>
